card.name: Jingle dress
card.tagline: Ojibwe healing powwow dance - MISFILED under India
card.profile: The Jingle Dress Dance is a First Nations and Native American women's powwow dance and regalia tradition of the Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) peoples of the Great Lakes region, NOT a South Asian dance (Wikipedia, Jingle dress; Parks Canada). Its origin is attributed to Ojibwe communities - Mille Lacs, the Red Lake Band of Chippewa and Whitefish Bay (Naotkamegwanning) - through a recurring dream given to a Midewinini (medicine man) whose gravely ill granddaughter was healed by dancing in a dress adorned with rows of metal cones (ziibaaska'iganan) (Wikipedia). University of Minnesota professor Brenda Child dates the dress and dance to circa 1918-19, tied to the 1918-19 influenza pandemic; it arose just as the U.S. Indian Office issued a circular banning ritual dancing (1921) (Univ. of Minnesota).
card.insight: Far from a 'party trick,' the jingle dress is a sacred healing tradition - dancers keep one foot connected to the earth and the sound of the cones is believed to carry prayers; it became an official powwow category after being popularised by Maggie White of Naotkamegwanning from the late 1960s (Parks Canada).
